title: Separate authentication middleware by credential class
objective: Resolve review feedback with direct user, project, organization, and service middleware so each service explicitly selects enabled authentication mechanisms.
verified_facts: The current branch introduced parallel Boundary constructors and a combined dependency container.
The repository already has user, project, organization, and service credential-specific middleware, but transport coverage is incomplete.
Multiple independently installed authenticators can overwrite the shared CTX_ value unless they reject an existing authenticated identity.
Credential selection and transport failures were distributed through small helper functions.
CodeQL reports callback logging of an error containing persisted or request-derived authentication data.
acceptance_criteria: User, project, organization, and service each have direct Gin, unary gRPC, and stream gRPC middleware constructors.
Existing constructor signatures remain unchanged; organization stream and service Gin constructors are the only new credential-specific APIs.

No Boundary, AuthenticationDependencies, credential-conflict constructor, private middleware wrapper, shared authentication function, credential-presence struct, count/class method, per-credential Gin reader, or response/log helper remains.

Each middleware ignores absent credentials, fails closed for malformed or rejected presented credentials, constructs the correct Authentication actor and scope, and rejects an already authenticated request before overwriting CTX_.
Service command wiring explicitly installs only the credential middleware classes that service accepts.

Assistant and Web install user, project, organization, and service middleware in that order for Gin, unary gRPC, and stream gRPC; Endpoint and Integration install the same ordered list for unary and stream gRPC and install no Gin authentication chain.
Gin source precedence remains exact: authorization path then header then query; x-auth-id and x-project-id header then path then query; scoped credentials header then query then path.
HTTP and gRPC failures use the capitalized generic message Invalid authentication credentials.
All middleware log messages begin with a capital letter and never include credential values.
Callback authentication reconstruction failures use a static capitalized log message without attaching the reconstruction error.
required_tests: Every credential class has Gin, unary, and stream success and rejection coverage.
Every credential middleware rejects an existing authenticated context when its own credential is presented.
Composed Gin, unary, and stream chains reject two presented credential classes in both normal and reversed middleware order before invoking handlers.
No-credential requests pass through every middleware variant.
Gin precedence tests cover user token, auth ID, selected project ID, project credential, organization credential, and service credential.
Gin, unary, and stream log-capture tests prove malicious credential values are absent from rejection and conflict logs.
Command wiring tests assert the exact per-service transport matrix and user-project-organization-service order, and reject Boundary and credential-conflict middleware.
Callback log tests prove malicious authentication metadata is absent.
delivery_gates: GitHub CodeQL analysis passes for the pushed commit.
GitHub aggregate CI Success check passes for the pushed commit.

principles.kiss: Expose one direct middleware per credential class and let service wiring state policy.
principles.yagni: Do not add dependency containers, policy registries, wrapper constructors, or generic authentication frameworks.
principles.single_ownership: Each credential middleware owns only its credential class; command wiring owns which classes a service accepts.
principles.explicit_contracts: Constructor names and service wiring make accepted credential classes visible.
principles.fail_safe: Presented invalid credentials and multiple enabled credentials fail before handlers run.
principles.observability: Capitalized failure categories remain actionable without credential or callback-derived values.
principles.least_privilege: A service authenticates only credential classes whose middleware it explicitly installs.
principles.reversibility: The change is code-only and can be reverted without schema or data rollback.

risks: Missing middleware in a command chain intentionally disables that credential class and must be caught by wiring tests.
Incorrect interceptor order must not permit a second credential to overwrite the first authenticated identity.
Adding transport parity can accidentally alter source precedence or legacy fail-open behavior.
Direct implementations duplicate small transport mechanics, so shared constants and complete tests are required to prevent message drift.
rollback: Revert the implementation commit to restore the prior Boundary implementation and command wiring. No persisted state changes are involved.
